title: PEAS
description: Power Electronics Agnostic Structure — Universal container for any electronic component. A valid MAS / CAS / SAS / RAS / controller / connector / analog document is also a valid PEAS.

inputs.description: Per-component design requirements and operating points. `designRequirements` is ALWAYS required — it is the ideal-simulation seed that the librarian uses to bind a real part and that is retained post-binding as the spec the part met. Its concrete shape is pinned to the discriminator branch (magnetic/capacitor/semiconductor/resistor/controller/connector/analog) by the if/then clauses at the bottom of this schema.

designRequirements.description: Family-specific design-requirements seed. The if/then clauses below pin this to the matching family schema based on which discriminator branch (magnetic/capacitor/semiconductor/resistor/controller/connector/analog) is populated.

operatingPoints.description: Operating points the component must satisfy. Shape is fixed by the sibling family schema (e.g. MAS inputs/operatingPoint).

outputs.description: Computed results (losses, thermal, impedance, etc.). May be a single object or an array of per-operating-point results; concrete shape is fixed by the sibling family schema.

oneOf.description: Magnetic component (inductor, transformer, choke) — defined by MAS.
Semiconductor (MOSFET, diode, IGBT, BJT) — defined by SAS.

Control IC (PWM / multiphase / LLC / PFC / phase-shift / sync-rectifier / digital / gate-driver / shunt-regulator / voltage-reference / current-sense / isolated amplifier / hot-swap / eFuse) — defined by CTAS. Extracted from the former inline PEAS branch into the CTAS sibling repo; CTAS owns the controller-family enums while reusing the PEAS shared primitives.

Connector — defined by CONAS. Covers the full range of board-boundary conductors: screw terminals (terminalBlock), solder pads, pin headers, edge-card, wire-to-board, RF, power, etc. A minimal Tier-1-only CONAS doc (connector: {}) with inputs.designRequirements (connectorFamily + electrical ratings) is valid for pre-librarian abstract-boundary seeds; manufacturerInfo is populated after librarian binding.

Analog IC (op amp, comparator, instrumentation/difference amp, PGA, buffer/line driver, sample-and-hold, analog switch, multiplexer, ADC, DAC) — generic analog/linear parts, defined by AAS. Distinct from CTAS (power-control ICs) and SAS (discrete power semiconductors).

Behavioral (mathematical model) component — a two-terminal element whose constitutive relation is expressed as an analytic formula or a parametric Chan saturable-core model. Simulator-agnostic: CiasCircuitConverter generates the correct syntax for each target (ngspice B-element with ddt(), LTspice FLux=/Q= or Hc/Bs/…, Verilog-A contribution statement).

allOf.$comment: Pin inputs.designRequirements shape to the populated discriminator branch.

behavioral.title: Behavioral
behavioral.description: A two-terminal element whose constitutive relation is given analytically. Two shapes: expression-based (flux linkage Ψ(i) or charge Q(v,i)) and the parametric Chan saturable-core model (Hc/Bs/Br + geometry). Variables in expressions are fixed by convention: i = port current [A], v = branch voltage [V], temp = temperature [°C]; standard math functions (exp, abs, sqrt, sin, cos, atan, log) are valid.

oneOf.description: Expression-based constitutive relation. nature='flux' defines Ψ(i)=expression [V·s]; nature='charge' defines Q(v,i)=expression [C]. CiasCircuitConverter emits: LTspice→FLux=/Q= with x=i or x=v; ngspice→B-element with V=ddt(expr(I(Vsense))) or I=ddt(expr(V(a,b))); Verilog-A→Phi(br)<+expr or Q(br)<+expr.

nature.description: Physical quantity being defined: 'flux' for flux-linkage Ψ(i) [V·s], 'charge' for charge Q(v,i) [C].

expression.description: Analytic expression using i (port current [A]), v (branch voltage [V]), and standard math functions. E.g. '1e-9*i*(12.897*exp(-0.04309*abs(i))+119.58*exp(-0.8347*abs(i)))'.

oneOf.description: Chan saturable core model (LTspice Hc/Bs/Br/A/Lm/Lg/N parameters). NOTE: despite widespread use of the name, LTspice implements the Chan 1991 model (IEEE Trans. CAD), not the Jiles-Atherton model — parameters are not inter-convertible without B-H curve fitting. CiasCircuitConverter emits: LTspice→L Hc=… Bs=… Br=… A=… Lm=… Lg=… N=…; ngspice→Chan/JA Verilog-A subcircuit (ngspice ≥36 via OSDI) or approximate saturation B-element; Verilog-A→Chan analog module.

coercive_force.description: Hc [A/m] — coercive field strength. The B-H material parameters (Hc/Bs/Br) may be temperature-dependent (LTspice tbl(temp,...)).

saturation_flux_density.description: Bs [T] — flux density at saturation. May be temperature-dependent.

remanence_flux_density.description: Br [T] — residual flux density after deenergisation. May be temperature-dependent.

magnetic_path_length.description: Lm [m] — mean magnetic path length of the core (geometry, NOT an inductance). LTspice Chan calls this Lm.

effective_area.description: A [m^2] — effective core cross-sectional area (geometry, NOT a domain density). LTspice Chan calls this A.

oneOf.description: Static nonlinear I-V (conductance) relation i(v) as a piecewise-linear table — e.g. a varistor/TVS/ESD clamping curve obtained by characterizing the device's terminals (model-order reduction of a behavioral macromodel). Points are strictly increasing in voltage; consumers interpolate. CiasCircuitConverter emits: ngspice -> B-source I=pwl(v(a,b), v1,i1, v2,i2, ...); LTspice -> behavioral current source with a table().

points.description: I-V breakpoints, strictly increasing in voltage.

voltage.description: Terminal voltage v across the device [V].

current.description: Current i through the device at v [A].

behavioralTemperatureValue.title: behavioralTemperatureValue
behavioralTemperatureValue.description: A scalar in a behavioral model that may vary with temperature. Either a plain number (temperature-independent) or a set of (temperature, value) breakpoints that reproduce the source LTspice tbl(temp, T1,v1, T2,v2, ...) table; consumers interpolate, and a non-interpolating consumer resolves at referenceTemperature.

referenceTemperature.description: Temperature in degrees Celsius at which a non-interpolating consumer should resolve this quantity (e.g. 25).

perTemperature.description: Breakpoints of the value versus temperature, reproducing the source tbl(temp, ...) table.
